header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue https://github.com/softwaremill/sttp/issues/3066 ("CurlBackend: errors lose libcurl's message and code").

Problem: in core/src/main/scalanative/sttp/client4/curl/AbstractCurlBackend.scala, when a curl transfer fails the exception message is only `s"Command failed with status ${curlCode.getOrElse(code)}"`. `CurlOption.ErrorBuffer` exists but is never set, so libcurl's own error text is lost. E.g. a self-signed cert and a wrong-host cert both yield `java.io.IOException: Command failed with status SSL_CACERT`, while curl itself reports "SSL certificate OpenSSL verify result: self-signed certificate (18)" vs "SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target hostname ...". Also `CurlCode` uses libcurl's pre-7.62 names: code 60 (today: any peer certificate verification failure) is named `SSL_CACERT`, and code 51 holds the name 60 should have.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Set `CURLOPT_ERRORBUFFER` (CurlOption.ErrorBuffer) per request, with a buffer of CURL_ERROR_SIZE (256) bytes, allocated so it stays valid for the whole transfer and is freed afterwards (follow the existing memory management patterns in the curl backend; no leaks).
2. On failure, the exception message includes the numeric libcurl code, sttp's name for it, and libcurl's error-buffer text when non-empty (fall back to curl_easy_strerror text or just the code/name if the buffer is empty). Keep the existing mapping of curl codes to sttp exception types (from #3046) unchanged.
3. Rename CurlCode entries 51 and 60 to libcurl's current names (51 = PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION -> check current libcurl naming: 51 is now CURLE_OBSOLETE51 / formerly PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION; 60 is CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION). Verify against libcurl's curl.h and update any references (including error-type mapping) accordingly.
4. Add/adjust tests for the Scala Native curl backend where feasible (e.g. message formatting unit test); the project's existing test layout under core/src/test/scalanative should be followed.
5. Code must compile for Scala Native: `sbt "compileScoped 3 Native"` and `sbt "compileScoped 2.13 Native"`; run relevant native tests with `sbt "testScoped 3 Native"` if the environment allows (curl native tests may need libcurl dev headers installed).

Keep the change minimal and focused on the issue.

resultJson.description:
Fixes softwaremill/sttp#3066. When a curl transfer fails in the Scala Native curl backend, the exception message is only `Command failed with status <name>`, so different failures with the same libcurl code (e.g. a self-signed certificate vs. a certificate for the wrong host, both code 60) can't be told apart. `CurlOption.ErrorBuffer` is defined but never set, so libcurl's own error text is thrown away.

The epic sets `CURLOPT_ERRORBUFFER` on every request with a 256-byte (CURL_ERROR_SIZE) buffer that lives as long as the easy handle, and builds the failure message from the numeric libcurl code, sttp's name for it, and libcurl's text (the error buffer if non-empty, otherwise `curl_easy_strerror`). The mapping of curl codes to Java exception types from #3046 stays exactly as it is — only the message changes.

It also renames two `CurlCode` entries to libcurl's current names (verified against curl's master `curl.h`): 51 is `CURLE_OBSOLETE51` ("NOT USED") and 60 is `CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION`; `CURLE_SSL_CACERT` is now only a `#define` alias for 60. Code 77 (`SSL_CACERT_BADFILE`) is still current and is not touched.

tasks.description:
In `core/src/main/scalanative/sttp/client4/curl/internal/CurlCode.scala`:
- line 56: `val PeerFailedVerification = Value(51, "PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION")` -> `val Obsolete51 = Value(51, "OBSOLETE51")` (matches the existing `ObsoleteNN` entries).
- line 65: `val SslCacert = Value(60, "SSL_CACERT")` -> `val PeerFailedVerification = Value(60, "PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION")`.

Do not touch 77 (`SSL_CACERT_BADFILE`), it is still the current name. Neither `SslCacert` nor `PeerFailedVerification` is referenced anywhere else in the repo (grep-verified: main, tests, docs, effects modules), and `AbstractCurlBackend.transferException` does not match on either code, so the exception-type mapping needs no change — both stay `IOException`.

Test: add a new Scala Native test file `core/src/test/scalanative/sttp/client4/CurlCodeTest.scala` (header `package sttp.client4` / `package curl`, `AnyFreeSpec with Matchers`, like the sibling curl tests) asserting `CurlCode(60).toString == "PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION"`, `CurlCode(51).toString == "OBSOLETE51"`, and that `AbstractCurlBackend.transferException(60)` is still a plain `java.io.IOException` whose message contains `PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION`. If the later task changes `transferException`'s signature, it updates this call.

Verify: `sbt "compileScoped 3 Native"`, `sbt "compileScoped 2.13 Native"`, and if the environment allows `STTP_NATIVE=1 sbt "coreNative/testOnly sttp.client4.curl.CurlCodeTest"`.

tasks.title: Set CURLOPT_ERRORBUFFER per request and include libcurl's code and text in transfer exceptions
tasks.description:
All in `core/src/main/scalanative/sttp/client4/curl/` (+ tests). See the brief for exact call sites.

1. Buffer allocation/ownership — tie it to `CurlSpaces`, which already holds the per-request malloc'd memory that outlives the transfer:
   - `internal/CurlSpaces.scala`: add a 4th field `val errorBuffer: Ptr[CChar]` (i.e. `CString`).
   - `AbstractCurlBackend.responseSpace`: allocate it with `calloc(256.toUInt, sizeof[CChar])` (zeroed, so it reads as empty if libcurl writes nothing). Put the size in a named constant, e.g. `private[curl] val CurlErrorSize = 256` in the `AbstractCurlBackend` companion, with a short comment that it is libcurl's CURL_ERROR_SIZE.
   - `AbstractCurlBackend.freeSpaces`: `free` it. Every existing cleanup path already calls `curl.cleanup()` before `freeSpaces(spaces)`; keep that order (libcurl requires the buffer to stay valid until the handle is cleaned up or the option is reset).
   - `send`: right after `val spaces = responseSpace`, call `curl.option(ErrorBuffer, spaces.errorBuffer)` (the `Ptr[?]` overload; `ErrorBuffer` is already in scope via `import CurlOption.{Header => _, _}`), before dispatching to `handleFile` / `handleBaseWithMulti` / `handleBase`.
   - `CurlMultiInputStream`: add a constructor parameter `errorBuffer: Ptr[CChar]` (place it before the defaulted `headerLists`), pass `spaces.errorBuffer` at the single construction site in `handleBaseWithMulti`, and `free` it in `close()` after `easyHandle.cleanup()` next to the other frees. Update the class scaladoc's ownership sentence.

2. `curl_easy_strerror` binding: in `internal/CCurl.scala` add `@name("curl_easy_strerror") def easyStrerror(code: CInt): CString = extern` (fixed signature, so a direct binding like `curl_easy_cleanup`; no `ffi.c` change). The returned string is static — never free it.

3. Message + exception, in the `AbstractCurlBackend` companion object:
   - Change `transferException(code: Int)` to `transferException(code: Int, errorBuffer: CString)`. It reads `fromCString(errorBuffer).trim` (treat a null pointer as empty); if empty, falls back to `fromCString(CCurl.easyStrerror(code))`; then builds the message and picks the exception type with the existing `curlCode match` — leave that match's cases byte-for-byte the same.
   - Extract the pure formatting into `private[curl] def transferErrorMessage(code: Int, name: Option[String], detail: String): String` so it can be unit-tested without native memory. Format: `curl error <code> (<NAME>): <detail>`; omit ` (<NAME>)` when the code is not in `CurlCode`, and omit `: <detail>` when detail is empty. Example: `curl error 60 (PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION): SSL certificate problem: self-signed certificate`.
   - Update the scaladoc of `transferException` to say what the message contains (usage-level, concise).

4. Call sites (5), each must read the buffer before it is freed — all already are, do not reorder cleanup:
   - private `perform(c: CurlHandle)` (line ~36): add a `spaces: CurlSpaces` parameter and pass `spaces.errorBuffer`; update its two callers in `handleBase` and `handleFile` (`.flatMap(_ => perform(curl, spaces))`). The error is created inside `flatMap`, before the `.ensure` cleanup runs.
   - `handleBaseWithMulti`: the two `throw AbstractCurlBackend.transferException(transferResult)` (lines ~287 and ~339); cleanup happens later in the outer `catch`.
   - `CurlMultiInputStream.read`: the two `transferError.foreach(code => throw ...)` (lines ~62 and ~76); `close()` frees the buffer later. `transferError = Some(-1)` (multi-level failure) keeps working: unknown code -> no name, `curl_easy_strerror(-1)` text.
   Leave `lift`/`liftM` (setopt / multi-op failures, `RuntimeException`) unchanged — out of scope.

5. Tests (ScalaTest, `core/src/test/scalanative/sttp/client4/`, header `package sttp.client4` / `package curl`):
   - New `CurlTransferExceptionTest.scala` (`AnyFreeSpec with Matchers`): `transferErrorMessage` for known code + detail, unknown code, empty detail; `transferException` with a `Zone`-allocated buffer (`toCString("some text")`) includes code, name and the text; with an empty buffer (`c""`) falls back to non-empty `curl_easy_strerror` text; exception types unchanged for 28 -> `SocketTimeoutException`, 6 and 5 -> `UnknownHostException`, 7 -> `ConnectException`, 1 and 3 -> `MalformedURLException`, 61 -> `UnsupportedEncodingException`, 60 -> `IOException`.
   - If the previous task's `CurlCodeTest` calls `transferException(60)`, update it to the new signature.
   - In `CurlBackendHttpTest.scala` add one end-to-end test under the existing `"curl backend" - { ... }` block: `basicRequest.get(uri"http://localhost:7918").send(backend)` (same refused port as HttpTest's "connection refused" test) fails with `SttpClientException.ConnectException` whose `getCause.getMessage` contains `curl error 7 (COULDNT_CONNECT)` and has non-empty text after it (don't assert libcurl's exact wording, it varies by version). Add the same for a streamed response (`.response(asInputStreamAlways(...))`) to cover the `handleBaseWithMulti` path.

Verify: `sbt "compileScoped 3 Native"`, `sbt "compileScoped 2.13 Native"` (also compiles `effects/cats` and `effects/zio` native backends, which extend `AbstractSyncCurlBackend` but need no change), then if the environment allows `STTP_NATIVE=1 sbt "testScoped 3 Native"` or narrower `STTP_NATIVE=1 sbt "coreNative/test"`. Run in the foreground; report as unverified if libcurl dev headers/clang are missing.

resultJson.brief:
## Scope
Scala Native curl backend only. Everything lives in the `core` module:
- `core/src/main/scalanative/sttp/client4/curl/` — backend (`AbstractCurlBackend.scala`, `CurlMultiInputStream.scala`, `CurlBackends.scala`)
- `core/src/main/scalanative/sttp/client4/curl/internal/` — FFI layer (`CCurl.scala` externs, `CurlApi.scala` typed wrappers, `CurlCode.scala`, `CurlOption.scala`, `CurlSpaces.scala`, `package.scala`)
- `core/src/main/resources/scala-native/ffi.c` — C shims, only for varargs functions (`curl_easy_setopt`/`getinfo`) and the write callback. Fixed-signature libcurl functions are bound directly in `CCurl.scala`.
- `core/src/test/scalanative/sttp/client4/` — native tests (`CurlBackendHttpTest.scala`, `CurlTryBackendHttpTest.scala`, `CurlMultiInputStreamTest.scala`). Curl tests in package `curl` use the two-line header `package sttp.client4` / `package curl` while sitting directly in that directory; follow that so `private[curl]` members are reachable.
- `effects/cats/src/main/scalanative/.../CurlCatsBackend.scala` and `effects/zio/src/main/scalanative/.../CurlZioBackend.scala` extend `AbstractSyncCurlBackend`; they only pass a monad, so no change is expected, but they must still compile.

## Verified libcurl facts (curl master `include/curl/curl.h`)
- `CURLE_OBSOLETE51, /* 51 - NOT USED */`
- `CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION, /* 60 - peer's certificate or fingerprint was not verified fine */`
- `CURLE_SSL_CACERT_BADFILE` = 77, still current.
- `#define CURLE_SSL_CACERT CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION` (old name is just an alias).
- `#define CURL_ERROR_SIZE 256`.
- `CURLOPT_ERRORBUFFER` = 10010 = existing `CurlOption.ErrorBuffer` (`Value(10000 + 10)`), never set today.
- The buffer must stay valid until `curl_easy_cleanup` (or the option is reset). libcurl may leave it empty on failure -> fall back to `const char *curl_easy_strerror(CURLcode)` (returns a static string, never free; no binding exists yet).

## Current code (AbstractCurlBackend.scala)
- `CurlCode` is a Scala `Enumeration` (`private[client4]`); `CurlCode(n)` throws for unknown ids, so lookups use `CurlCode.values.find(_.id == code)`. `toString` gives the name string, e.g. `COULDNT_CONNECT`.
- Companion `object AbstractCurlBackend`: `private[curl] def transferException(code: Int): Exception` builds `s"Command failed with status ${curlCode.getOrElse(code)}"` and maps: `OperationTimedOut` -> `SocketTimeoutException`; `CouldntResolveHost | CouldntResolveProxy` -> `UnknownHostException`; `CouldntConnect` -> `ConnectException`; `UnsupportedProtocol | UrlMalformat` -> `MalformedURLException`; `BadContentEncoding` -> `UnsupportedEncodingException`; else `IOException`. This mapping (from #3046) must not change. `send` wraps everything in `SttpClientException.adjustExceptions`, so users see `SttpClientException.ConnectException/ReadException/TimeoutException` with the above as `getCause`.
- 5 call sites of `transferException`: private `perform(c: CurlHandle): F[CurlCode]` (line ~36, used by `handleBase` and `handleFile` as `.flatMap(_ => perform(curl))`); two `throw`s in `handleBaseWithMulti` (lines ~287, ~339); two in `CurlMultiInputStream.read` (lines ~62, ~76, via `transferError: Option[Int]`, which is `Some(-1)` for multi-level failures).
- Note the name clash: inside `send` there is a local `def perform(implicit ctx: Context)`; the class-level private `perform(c: CurlHandle)` is the one that calls `performCurl`.
- `lift(code)` / `liftM(code)` raise `RuntimeException` for failed setopt / multi operations — unrelated to transfer errors, leave alone.

## Memory management patterns
- Per-request native memory that must outlive the transfer is `malloc`/`calloc`'d (libc `stdlib`, already imported) and held in `CurlSpaces(bodyResp: Ptr[CurlFetch], headersResp: Ptr[CurlFetch], httpCode: Ptr[Long])`, created by `private def responseSpace` and released by `private def freeSpaces(spaces)`. `calloc(4096.toUInt, sizeof[CChar])` is the existing allocation idiom.
- Every cleanup path does `curl.cleanup()` then `freeSpaces(spaces)`: `.ensure(...)` in `handleBase`/`handleFile`, the early-return in `handleFile` when `fopen` fails, and the fallback + outer `catch` in `handleBaseWithMulti` (guarded by `resourcesCleaned`).
- Streaming path: ownership of the individual pointers (not the `CurlSpaces` object) moves to `new CurlMultiInputStream(multi, curl, spaces.bodyResp, spaces.headersResp, spaces.httpCode, detachedHeaders)`, whose `close()` does `removeHandle`, `easyHandle.cleanup()`, `multiHandle.cleanup()`, then frees each pointer. Its constructor is `private[curl]` and has a single construction site, so adding a parameter is safe. Anything added to `CurlSpaces` must also be handed over and freed there, or it leaks.
- The `Zone` in `Context` is closed when `send`'s effect completes, which is before a streamed response is read — so zone-allocated memory is NOT valid for the whole transfer on the streaming path. Do not allocate the error buffer in the zone.
- `send` creates `val spaces = responseSpace` just before dispatching to `handleFile` / `handleBaseWithMulti` / `handleBase`; that is the one place all three paths share.

## FFI helpers
- `CurlApi.CurlHandleOps.option(option: CurlOption, parameter: Ptr[?]): CurlCode` -> `sttp_curl_setopt_pointer`. Use it to set `ErrorBuffer`.
- `CCurl` is `libcurlPlatformCompat.instance` (a `val` in `internal/package.scala`, `private[curl]`), an `@extern trait CCurl`; add direct bindings as `@name("curl_...") def x(...): T = extern`.
- `fromCString` / `toCString` (needs implicit `Zone`) / `c"..."` literals come from `scala.scalanative.unsafe._`.

## Tests
- ScalaTest. `HttpTest[F]` (shared, `core/src/test/scala/sttp/client4/testing/HttpTest.scala`) is async and already asserts exception types for curl: unknown host and `http://localhost:7918` (connection refused) -> `SttpClientException.ConnectException`, read errors, timeouts. No existing test asserts on the `Command failed with status` text (grep-verified in tests and docs), so changing the message breaks nothing.
- Backend-specific sync tests go in `CurlBackendHttpTest` under `"curl backend" - { ... }`; standalone specs use `AnyFreeSpec with Matchers` (see `CurlMultiInputStreamTest`). `HttpTest.endpoint` is the local test server, started automatically by `testServerSettings`.
- Don't assert libcurl's exact error wording — it differs between libcurl versions and TLS backends. Assert code, sttp name, and that some text follows.

## Build
- Compile: `sbt "compileScoped 3 Native"`, `sbt "compileScoped 2.13 Native"`.
- Tests: `sbt "testScoped 3 Native"`. Native projects are only aggregated when env var `STTP_NATIVE` is set (`STTP_NATIVE=1`); needs clang, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libidn2-dev. Scala 3 native project id is `coreNative` (2.13: `coreNative2_13`), e.g. `STTP_NATIVE=1 sbt "coreNative/testOnly sttp.client4.curl.CurlTransferExceptionTest"`.
- sbt 2 gotchas: pass several commands as one `;`-joined argument (`sbt -batch "a" "b"` runs only the first); native test `println` output is not shown by sbt; if a recompile fails with `AccessDeniedException` on `.nir` files, `rm -rf target/out/native0.5/*/core` and retry; after deleting/renaming sources, stale outputs can cause native link errors — `sbt shutdown` then remove `target/out/native0.5/scala-3.*/core`.
- Code must compile on Scala 2.12/2.13/3: no Scala-3-only syntax beyond what the file already uses (`using` in call position and `?` wildcards are already used there).

## Conventions
- Keep the change minimal; no unrelated refactors. No docs mention the old message or `SSL_CACERT`, so no docs change.
- Comments: short, only non-obvious facts (e.g. why the buffer is calloc'd outside the zone); scaladoc describes usage, not implementation.
- Do not commit; never add a Claude co-author.
